annotations.coverageReview: Visible front and side survey images and final four-patch overlays inspected. Azure Kirin upper cheek, muzzle, lower chin and side jaw cover actual anatomy. The side-jaw radius was expanded from .08 to .10 after the original battle patch retained only 14 vertices; the final reviewed patch has 30 and stays on the snout. Mane, antlers, tail and limbs still need all-clip and technique review.

review.name: Azure Kirin
findings: All 13 source clips actually inspected in 12 enlarged face/body front/side slices. Subtle snout and cheek shear when the head turns in alternate idle, strike and defeat. Four limbs, mane, tail and antlers remain connected in raw clips; equipped-technique coordination still pending. The corresponding battle face/body slices were also actually inspected; the same facial problem is present and there are no additional detached body surfaces in these raw clips. Equipped-technique review remains open.

companionTechniqueAudit.label: independent-legendary-005-techniques-v1
companionTechniqueAudit.finding: All nine actual equipped techniques were selected and played through the production companion stage. All 36 front/side sheets were actually inspected, covering windup, strike, recovery and return to idle. Snout, mane, tail and limbs remain connected; stronger strikes rear and tuck as a coherent whole body motion, support moves remain compact, and guard returns without a snap. Production runtime and live release verification remain pending.

All 13 source clips actually inspected in 12 enlarged face/body front/side slices. Beak curvature changes slightly on raised attack/cast; independent exposed-beak probe detects drift that the previous broad mask missed. Wings frequently occlude the side face, but front views retain coverage; claws, feathers and body remain connected. Recheck beak after conservative face repair; actual techniques pending. The corresponding battle face/body slices were also actually inspected; the same facial problem is present and there are no additional detached body surfaces in these raw clips. Equipped-technique review remains open. Separate candidate only. Bind the complete measured face to head with a smooth neck fade; preserve geometry, clips and accessories outside the measured region. First candidate rejected: face probe passed but full-body geometry detected 25 wing seam warnings from the face fade touching forward wing feathers. Narrowed the lateral repair extent to keep the measured beak/face and exclude those original wing vertices.

All 13 source clips actually inspected in 12 enlarged face/body front/side slices. Lower snout/cheek moves relative to upper head, most visible in raised strike and turned defeat. Long whiskers flex as accessories and must remain free. Limbs, body and tail remain connected in raw clips; actual techniques pending. The corresponding battle face/body slices were also actually inspected; the same facial problem is present and there are no additional detached body surfaces in these raw clips. Equipped-technique review remains open. Separate candidate only. Bind the complete measured face to head with a smooth neck fade; preserve geometry, clips and accessories outside the measured region.

All 13 source clips actually inspected in 12 enlarged face/body front/side slices. Clear lower-mouth collapse during early recoil (12.5%) and lower jaw/cheek shear in strike and turned defeat. Mane, scarf and tail require preservation. Raw forelegs fold forward during strike/recoil; actual technique and planted-paw coordination specifically remain open. The corresponding battle face/body slices were also actually inspected; the same facial problem is present and there are no additional detached body surfaces in these raw clips. Equipped-technique review remains open. Separate candidate only. Bind the complete measured face to head with a smooth neck fade; preserve geometry, clips and accessories outside the measured region. First candidate rejected visually despite independent face and whole-body geometry passing: chin-to-beard transition showed stripes and stretched fur in turned defeat and victory. Expand the rigid beard region and spread the lower neck fade; no approval until new complete visuals and body checks pass. V3 rejected visually: the broad depth fade touched chest and collar surfaces. V4 retains the lower beard extent but restores the conservative forward-depth and lateral limits; chest must remain behind the repair.
